summary.value: Use `Heading` to render h1-6 elements with heading text styles.

a11y.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.rule: Use correct heading levels (h1-h6) for proper semantic structure
value.quote: Make sure to use correct heading levels (h1-h6) to ensure proper semantic structure.

value.rule: Starting headings with keywords makes scanning and locating information easier
value.quote: Starting headings with keywords makes it easier for everyone to scan the page and locate relevant information.

value.rule: The h1 must describe the entire page; subheadings must be unique and indicate their section's content
value.quote: The main page heading — the <h1> element — must describe the entire page, while each subheading should be unique and clearly indicate what the following section contains.

value.rule: Use headings in the correct order (h1-h6) for a clear, predictable structure
value.quote: Use headings in the correct order ( h1 - h6 ) to create a clear and predictable structure.

value.rule: Coherent, logical heading hierarchy is essential since many users navigate by skimming headings
value.quote: Many users navigate by skimming the headings, and it is therefore essential that the hierarchy is coherent and provides a logical division of the content.

value.rule: A tidy heading structure helps assistive technologies present the page correctly
value.quote: A tidy heading structure also makes it easier for assistive technologies to present the page correctly.

value.rule: Avoid skipping heading levels in the hierarchy
value.quote: Avoid skipping levels in the hierarchy.

value.rule: Jumping heading levels (e.g. h2 to h4) makes content organisation harder to understand, unlike natural progressions (e.g. h2 to h3)
value.quote: Moving from <h2> to <h3> is natural, while jumping from <h2> to <h4> can make it harder to understand how the content is organised.

value.rule: Be consistent with heading structure across pages and sections in your solution
value.quote: Be consistent across pages and sections in your solution.

value.rule: A given heading level's structure (e.g. table of contents at h2) should apply everywhere
value.quote: If a table of contents uses <h2> in one place, the same structure should apply everywhere.

value.rule: Visual style and semantic HTML should match for the corresponding heading level
value.quote: Both the visual style and the semantic HTML should be the same for the corresponding heading level.

value.rule: Consistent heading structure helps users build a stable mental model of content organisation
value.quote: This helps users build a stable mental model of how the content is organised.

value.rule: Heading is used to establish structure and hierarchy in content
value.quote: Heading is used to establish structure and hierarchy in content.

value.rule: Use headings to divide information into clear, logical sections
value.quote: Use headings to divide information into clear, logical sections.

value.rule: Headings and subheadings should be short and clear, giving readers an accurate idea of the content they introduce
value.quote: Headings and subheadings should be short and clear, giving readers an accurate idea of the content they introduce.
